values.note: 'There are no hookups for RVs, but small to midsize camping trailers will fit into most of the sites'; 'all sites are suitable for tent or trailer camping'.

facilities.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10344825 ('two vault toilets, trash service, and a hand water pump') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/recreation/day-run-campground ('Vault Toilet'; 'Potable water is not available at this site'), read 2026-10-21

note: High-elevation campground just off the Highland Scenic Highway; many of its sites border the upper scenic Williams River.  --AWH

summary: Confirmed $15/night (rec.gov FCFS rate), 12 sites, no hookups, vault toilets. Booking changed to first-come only, not reservable, 14-night max (overrides the inherited rec.gov reservable row). Drinking water left unrecorded: rec.gov lists a hand pump, the FS page says no potable water. Not stated: rig length beyond 'small to midsize camping trailers', season (rec.gov's FCFS season Apr 20 - Oct 31, 2026 is a rate season). Run by the Forest Service's Marlinton-White Sulphur Ranger District (no concessioner named).
flags: Missing agency website: the Forest Service page https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/recreation/day-run-campground (the entry has only the recreation.gov page, which takes no reservations here).
Missing phone: recreation.gov gives (304) 799-4334 for facility information (Marlinton ranger district).
Inherited federal booking row (reservable via recreation.gov, 180-day window) is wrong here; this result overrides it with first-come only.
Criteria (soft): recreation.gov says only 'small to midsize camping trailers will fit into most of the sites'; no length is posted.

Road caveat: the directions use FR 86 from WV 150 to FR 216; the Forest Service closed FR 86 'from the intersection of FR 216 to the intersection with WV Route 150' from July 20, 2026 for flood repair, and Forest Order 09-21-02-26-04 keeps closures shifting along FR 86 through Nov 30, 2026. The FS says recreation sites stay reachable from Dyer to the west.
